findings.claim: FRANK historically contained 2106 Titan long-term-memory nodes while the agent still reported that it could not access its persistent profile because there was no active memory_recall path. Storage existence did not imply cognitive availability.
findings.current_implication: Memory success must be measured end-to-end as query/retrieval -> workspace availability -> decision/effect -> outcome/re-entry, not by stored-node counts or database presence.

findings.claim: Entity-session conversations were durably stored in their own SQLite databases and transcripts but were not ingested into Titan or meaningful chat_memory records, so they were not recallable across sessions until explicit bridge ingestion was added.
findings.current_implication: Logical memory unification requires explicit ingestion/query visibility and identity/provenance across stores. Physical persistence in isolated databases is insufficient.

findings.claim: A later MemoryHub provided one logical query across chat, Titan, consciousness, world and preferences while retaining distinct underlying stores, using RRF fusion, recency-aware budget packing, source attribution, retrieval metrics and a consistency daemon.
findings.current_implication: This is concrete historical support for current UnifiedDB's semantic/logical unification model: one identity/query plane does not require an unconditional physical single-database merge.

findings.claim: Titan graph repair found 6675 orphaned edges with 0 nodes. Recovery introduced foreign-key enforcement, ON DELETE CASCADE, node protection, re-ingestion, crash-safe embedding backfill and periodic consistency checks.
findings.current_implication: ClayGraph/UnifiedDB acceptance needs referential-integrity, orphan detection, crash/restart replay, resumable backfill, consistency audit and repair receipts as first-class invariants.

findings.claim: The LCME tuning commit reports retrieval P@5 improving from 0.40 to 1.00 after removing 7213 entity vectors, filtering EN/DE stop words, heavily weighting relevance, gating immature neural retrieval components, disabling graph expansion by default and enabling HNSW above 500 vectors.
findings.current_implication: More graph expansion/vectors/neural retrieval is not monotonically better. Each retrieval layer should earn activation through held-out precision/recall/latency tests and cold-start gates.

findings.claim: Titan was renamed to LCME across 42 files while durable DB filenames and tool names were deliberately preserved for data safety and LoRA compatibility, with a backwards-compatible redirect.
findings.current_implication: Semantic/runtime migrations should preserve stable durable identities and learned interfaces or provide explicit reversible versioned migration contracts rather than silently renaming semantic resources.

findings.claim: Historical memory recovery used crash-safe cursor state for embedding backfill, automatic DB reconnect, per-query source/latency/injected-size metrics and periodic consistency cleanup.
findings.current_implication: Long-running cognitive persistence should expose resumable jobs, explicit cursors, recovery idempotence and observability instead of best-effort hidden maintenance.

earned_work_mappings.mechanism_or_result: Logical federated memory query, active recall-path semantics, source attribution and memory-visibility failure modes already have historical implementation evidence.
earned_work_mappings.falsifier_or_validation_receipt: UnifiedDB/Harness must demonstrate cross-store identity-preserving recall with source provenance and a causal effect receipt under matched retrieval tests.

earned_work_mappings.mechanism_or_result: Orphan graph corruption, inaccessible stored memory, isolated-store recall loss and crash-recovery behavior provide concrete persistence/recovery regression tests.
earned_work_mappings.falsifier_or_validation_receipt: Harness must reproduce orphaning, restart/backfill interruption, isolated-store memory and unavailable recall-path failures against the new implementation.

earned_work_mappings.mechanism_or_result: Historical precision tuning, cold-start gating, HNSW thresholding, graph-expansion ablation and compatibility-preserving migration form reusable retrieval benchmark/migration scaffolding.
earned_work_mappings.falsifier_or_validation_receipt: Held-out ClayGraph/UnifiedDB retrieval suite must verify precision/recall/latency and migration compatibility; graph expansion or learned retrieval remains disabled if it does not beat the simpler baseline.

progress_accounting.reason: Combined denominator remains unfrozen; Drive archive internals are inaccessible through the current connector and Project-Frankenstein exact history-aware manifest remains incomplete.

branch_feedback.unifieddb: Historical MemoryHub is direct evidence that one logical query/identity plane can federate multiple physical stores. Require explicit visibility, source provenance, transactions/recovery and cross-store identity; do not equate unification with forced physical merge.
branch_feedback.claygraph: Graph/vector expansion polluted retrieval historically; keep graph expansion and learned retrieval behind held-out precision/recall gates. Make referential integrity and temporal provenance mandatory.
branch_feedback.harness: Add regression fixtures for 6675-orphan graph corruption, stored-but-unreachable memory, isolated-store cross-session loss, crash-safe backfill resume, DB reconnect, retrieval-layer ablation and migration compatibility.
branch_feedback.frank: Memory counts are not cognition. Require end-to-end memory availability receipts from retrieval through workspace effect/outcome/re-entry.
branch_feedback.claycode: Stable durable resource identity and learned tool-interface compatibility should survive implementation renames through versioned migration contracts.
branch_feedback.gwt: A memory only becomes globally useful when it is causally available to selection/broadcast/effect; storage presence alone is not workspace availability.
branch_feedback.clay: Reuse the federation/recovery/measurement principles, not the historical Titan/LCME topology as a mandatory final design.
